defects.description: Russia's over 800 million hectares is called 'about two-fifths of the global total', but 800 million is one-fifth of the world's roughly 4 billion hectares, not two-fifths.
paraphrases: 800 million is one-fifth of 4 billion, not two-fifths.
Two-fifths of 4 billion would be 1.6 billion hectares, not 800 million.
The stated share is double what the hectare figures imply.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'about one-fifth' (800M / 4B). Findable from the 4 billion total and Russia's 800 million, distinct.

defects.description: Forest is said to be a little over one-third of habitable land and 'around one-half of all land', but habitable land is a subset of all land, so one-third of habitable land must be less than one-third of all land, not one-half of it.
paraphrases: One-third of habitable land cannot be half of the larger total land.
Since habitable land is only part of all land, the forest share of all land must be smaller than its share of habitable land.
The share of total land is overstated relative to the habitable-land share.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'around one-quarter' (one-third of habitable land is about a quarter of all land). Findable from the subset relationship in the text, distinct.

defects.description: Russia is stated to hold the largest share at over 800 million hectares, yet Brazil (the only OTHER country above 10%) is also given 'over 800 million hectares', which would tie or exceed the country said to be largest.
paraphrases: Brazil cannot have over 800 million hectares if Russia is the largest at 800 million.
The second-ranked country is given as much forest as the first-ranked one.
Brazil's hectare figure contradicts its being smaller than Russia.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'over 400 million hectares' (more than 10% of 4 billion, and below Russia's 800M). Findable from Russia being the largest and Brazil being second, distinct.
